purpose: Classify FlowDocs demos, React islands, manual interactions, and local QA harnesses so component bugs are not confused with docs demo bugs.
rules: Package-owned React tests define component behavior truth.
Local component QA harnesses are human review tools and must stay outside the repo.
FlowDocs demos may demonstrate composition but must not own component logic, keyboard semantics, or state truth.
Any docs demo wrapper that adds state or interaction must be labelled as an adapter, not proof that the component works.
Pattern/template demos can compose components, but component-level defects must be fixed in package source and package tests first.

findings.issue: FlowDocs owns stateful island wrappers for components such as input, checkbox, combobox, select and country selector.
findings.action: These wrappers are acceptable only as docs harness adapters; package behavior must be tested in package-owned tests and local QA harnesses.

findings.issue: At least one local QA file may not prove React runtime directly.
findings.action: For each component QA harness, record whether it imports React runtime, generated docs runtime, or static markup.

findings.issue: Local QA harnesses include their own layout CSS.
findings.action: Keep them local and out of repo; use them for human inspection, not as component source truth.
